title: Reconcile QA role doc with moe-qa-loop skill on waiting for the completion commit
description: docs/roles/qa.md line 8 tells QA 'Do NOT wait' for task.commits and to stage/land the row's own paths itself, while docs/skills/moe-qa-loop/SKILL.md step 3 says an empty task.commits 'means the evidence is not yet verifiable ... wait for it before reviewing' and never review the dirty shared tree. Agents load both, so QA behaviour is currently whichever text it read last. Pick ONE rule and make both documents state it. Recommended interim rule until the Wave 1 finalize/candidate work lands: wait a bounded time (e.g. poll get_context for task.commits up to ~2 minutes) because the wrapper lands seconds after REVIEW; only if nothing arrives, fall back to the role doc's measured-attribution self-landing procedure, and say so in the qa_approve summary. Keep docs/roles/qa.md under the 40-line lint cap; put the long procedure in qa.reference.md. Role docs reach IDE users only via daemon prebuild + plugin rebuild, so also regenerate packages/moe-daemon/src/generated/initFiles.ts (npm run build). Source: roadmap 2026-09-10 §2.
definitionOfDone: docs/roles/qa.md and docs/skills/moe-qa-loop/SKILL.md give the same instruction for an empty task.commits, including the bounded wait and the fallback
npm run lint (role-doc linter) passes with qa.md at or under 40 lines
A daemon test or doc test asserts the two documents do not contain the contradictory phrases ('Do NOT wait' vs 'wait for it before reviewing') — or an equivalent guard
Rationale recorded in docs/roles/qa.reference.md pointing at the 2026-09-06 measurement (one completion in three reached REVIEW with bytes only in the dirty tree)

implementationPlan.description:
Add the guard test FIRST and confirm it is RED against the current docs. Create `packages/moe-daemon/src/util/qaCommitPolicy.test.ts` (vitest, ESM, mirror the import style of the sibling `initFiles.test.ts`: `import { ROLE_DOCS } from '../generated/initFiles.js'` and `import { SKILL_FILES } from '../generated/skillFiles.js'`).

Define two shared constants at the top of the file:
  const FORBIDDEN = ['Do NOT wait', 'wait for it before reviewing'];
  const SENTINELS = ['bounded wait, not a blocker', 'up to ~2 minutes', 'land it yourself', 'record_commit'];

Subjects under test — four texts:
  a) ROLE_DOCS['qa.md']
  b) SKILL_FILES['moe-qa-loop/SKILL.md']
  c) the same two files read from disk at `path.resolve(__dirname, '..', '..', '..', '..', 'docs', ...)` (src/util -> src -> moe-daemon -> packages -> repo root), LF-normalized with `.replace(/\r\n/g, '\n')` before any comparison.

Assertions:
  1. For each of the four texts: every FORBIDDEN literal is absent. Use an explicit per-phrase assertion so the failure message names the offending phrase and file, e.g. `expect(text, `${label} still carries "${phrase}"`).not.toContain(phrase)`.
  2. For each of the four texts: every SENTINEL is present. This positive half is what fails if a future edit deletes the rule instead of restating it, and what fails if a generated file is stale (the generated copy would still hold the old text).
  3. ROLE_DOCS['qa.reference.md'] contains '2026-09-06' and 'one completion in three' (DoD item 5's rationale anchor).
  4. Both generated keys exist and are non-empty — this is the error handling that stops a renamed skill directory or a dropped ROLE_DOCS key from silently turning every other assertion into a vacuous pass on `undefined`. Assert presence explicitly before reading the text, so the failure says 'key missing' instead of throwing a bare TypeError.
  5. Matching error handling for the on-disk half: compute `const hasDocs = fs.existsSync(docsRoot)` once and gate those cases with `it.skipIf(!hasDocs)` so the Docker build context (which ships only `packages/moe-daemon`) skips rather than dying on ENOENT — the same condition both generator scripts already handle by exiting 0.

Do NOT assert full-text equality between source and generated: the generators prepend an HTML-comment marker to role docs but inject a YAML-comment marker INSIDE the SKILL.md frontmatter, so exact equality is brittle for no added coverage. Substring parity on the policy text is the guard.

Run `npx vitest run src/util/qaCommitPolicy.test.ts` from `packages/moe-daemon` and record in the step note that it FAILS, naming which phrases tripped — the epic rail requires a test that fails on the old behaviour.

Write the canonical rule into `docs/roles/qa.md` and move the long procedure plus its rationale into `docs/roles/qa.reference.md`.

In qa.md, replace the whole of line 8 (the `Audit task.commits` bullet) with ONE bullet — keep the file's one-long-bullet-per-rule style so the line count barely moves:

- Audit `task.commits` from `get_context` — review the recorded completion commit (`git show <sha>`, `git branch --contains <sha>`), never the dirty shared tree. An empty `task.commits` at REVIEW is a bounded wait, not a blocker: re-run `task.verification` and the tests first, then re-poll `get_context` — up to ~2 minutes total, because the wrapper lands seconds after REVIEW. If a completion commit arrives, review that. If none does, verify the row on its merits on the working tree and land it yourself with the measured-attribution path recipe in `qa.reference.md` — then `moe.record_commit`, then approve, saying in the `qa_approve` summary that you self-landed after the bounded wait expired. A `NO-COMPLETION-COMMIT` warning after that is a daemon race, not a defect.

That bullet carries all four sentinels the guard test looks for and drops the phrase 'Do NOT wait'. Do not reintroduce that literal anywhere in the file.

In qa.reference.md, add a new section after 'Review order (do not skip)' titled `## Empty \`task.commits\` at REVIEW`. It holds three things:
  1. The rule restated in full (bounded wait, then fallback, then record_commit, then say so in the approve summary).
  2. The measured-attribution path recipe MOVED VERBATIM out of qa.md — the per-path `git diff -- <path> | grep '^[+-]' | grep -v '^[+-][+-]' | grep -vi '<row vocabulary>'` must-be-EMPTY check, the rule that a path also carrying a peer's hunks is EXCLUDED WHOLE because the peer's own landing carries it, that partial-hunk staging is a last resort needing a bare commit, and the task trailer + `moe.record_commit` finish. Do not reword or 'improve' this recipe — the governor ruling keeps it canonical.
  3. Rationale: measured 2026-09-06, one completion in three reached REVIEW with its bytes only in the dirty tree, because a wrapper lands a row only when its CLI process exits on that row — a session that hopped to another row, or an interactive seat that never exits, can never fire it. Record that `docs/roles/qa.md` (269d3fe, 2026-09-06) supersedes `docs/skills/moe-qa-loop/SKILL.md` (bf3f8fa, 2026-08-29) per the governor ruling, and that this is the interim rule until the Wave 1 finalize/candidate work lands.

Also reconcile the third statement of the same policy: item 3 of 'Review order (do not skip)' currently says 'Fall back to the working tree only when no commit exists, and then expect — and act on — the `qa_approve` `NO-COMPLETION-COMMIT` warning.' Replace that sentence with a pointer to the new section so the reference doc does not contradict itself.

qa.reference.md is exempt from the 40-line cap; qa.md is not. Run `npm run lint` from the repo root (Git Bash) or `scripts/lint-role-docs.ps1` and confirm qa.md is at or under 40 lines.

Reconcile `docs/skills/moe-qa-loop/SKILL.md` to the same rule. Six edits, all in that one file.

1. Step 3 of 'The decision flow' (line 18): delete the sentence 'An empty `task.commits` means the evidence is not yet verifiable: the wrapper lands the commit seconds after REVIEW, so wait for it before reviewing.' Replace it with the same rule qa.md now states, using the SAME four sentinel phrases verbatim ('bounded wait, not a blocker', 'up to ~2 minutes', 'land it yourself', `moe.record_commit`), and point at `.moe/roles/qa.reference.md` for the path-scoping recipe. Keep 'Do not review the dirty shared working tree — other sessions' edits live there too' as the rule for the normal case, but make it explicit that the self-landing fallback is the one sanctioned exception and that it is scoped to paths measured to be this row's own.

2. Make the ordering carry the wait: step 2 already re-runs `task.verification`, so state in step 3 that the re-poll happens after that re-run rather than as an idle sleep. Do not introduce a sleep loop.

3. 'Approve when' (line 40): change 'task.commits contains a completion commit recorded for this review round and reachable from the shared branch' to also accept the commit QA landed itself after the bounded wait expired.

4. 'Reject when' (line 51): this bullet currently rejects whenever no completion commit exists and the landing had time to run. That is now wrong — the fallback is to land it, not to reject. Narrow it to the case where the bytes genuinely are not there or cannot be attributed: no owned paths, or every dirty path also carries a peer's hunks so the whole-path exclusion leaves nothing to land. Keep the existing `lastCommitOutcome` refused/failed signal as evidence for that case. This bullet is the error handling for a fallback that legitimately cannot run — without it the reconciled flow would have no defined exit when self-landing refuses.

5. The approve paragraph (line 46) says a `NO-COMPLETION-COMMIT` warning is 'expected only with autoCommit off or when you approved inside the post-flight race; otherwise you should have rejected'. Change the tail to 'otherwise you should have landed it yourself first'.

6. Frontmatter `allowed-tools`: the skill currently permits only read-only git (`git diff`, `git log`, `git show`, `git branch`), which makes the canonical fallback unexecutable from inside the skill. Add the minimum needed to run the recipe: `Bash(git add:*)`, `Bash(git commit:*)`, `Bash(git status:*)`, `Bash(git rev-parse:*)`. Add nothing broader — no bare `Bash(git:*)`, no push.

Do not touch the oversized-diff, review-depth, reject-quality, or 'what never to do' sections — they are out of scope.

Regenerate both vendored artifacts and turn the guard test green.

From `packages/moe-daemon`, run the two generators DIRECTLY — not `npm run build` and not `npm run prebuild`, both of which run `npm run clean` and delete dist/ out from under anything using this shared checkout:

    npm run generate-init-files
    npm run generate-skill-files

They emit byte-identical output to what prebuild would produce. `generate-init-files` rewrites ROLE_DOCS['qa.md'] and ROLE_DOCS['qa.reference.md'] with fresh sha markers in `src/generated/initFiles.ts`; `generate-skill-files` rewrites SKILL_FILES['moe-qa-loop/SKILL.md'] in `src/generated/skillFiles.ts`. Check each command's exit code — both scripts print a skip message and exit 0 when their source docs directory is missing, so a silent 'skipped' is a real failure mode here and must not be mistaken for success.

Sanity-check the diff before moving on: `git diff --stat -- packages/moe-daemon/src/generated/` should show changes confined to those three embedded blocks plus their sha marker lines. Both generated files were verified in sync with their sources at plan time, so any OTHER doc appearing in the diff means something unrelated drifted — stop and report it in the step note rather than committing it.

Then verify, from `packages/moe-daemon`:

    npx vitest run src/util/qaCommitPolicy.test.ts src/util/initFiles.test.ts src/util/skillFiles.test.ts
    npx tsc --noEmit

All three suites must pass. `qaCommitPolicy.test.ts` was red at the first step and must now be green — that transition is the evidence the epic rail asks for; quote both results in the step note. `tsc --noEmit` typechecks the regenerated template literals without emitting into dist/.

Finally re-run the role-doc linter from the repo root and record that qa.md is at or under 40 lines.

Regression pass and adversarial self-review, then complete.

Regression: run the full daemon suite from `packages/moe-daemon` with `npm test` (vitest run). Nothing here touches daemon runtime code, so a green full suite is the expected result; a failure elsewhere is either pre-existing or a real regression — say which, with the failing test names, in the completion summary. Run `npm run lint` from the repo root one more time.

Adversarial review — walk these explicitly and answer each in the step note:
  - Do all four texts (qa.md source, its generated copy, SKILL.md source, its generated copy) now give the SAME instruction for an empty `task.commits`? Read them side by side; the guard test checks phrases, not meaning.
  - Does any of the three docs still contradict the rule somewhere the guard does not look? Specifically re-read qa.reference.md 'Review order' item 3, the SKILL's 'Approve when' / 'Reject when' lists, and the SKILL's approve paragraph.
  - Is the fallback executable by a QA seat as written — does `allowed-tools` now permit every command the recipe names?
  - Is there defined error handling for every exit of the new flow: commit arrives during the wait, no owned paths to stage, every dirty path peer-contaminated, `record_commit` itself failing? Each must lead somewhere the doc names, not to a dead end.
  - Two QA seats reviewing different rows at once: does the path-scoping recipe still keep them from committing each other's bytes? (It should — the whole-path exclusion for peer-touched files is exactly that guard. Confirm the moved text kept it.)
  - What if `task.commits` arrives DURING the bounded wait, after QA already staged paths? The rule must read as re-poll-then-decide, not stage-then-poll.

Hygiene: this checkout is shared and had 9 foreign dirty paths at plan time, plus `packages/moe-daemon/src/generated/initFiles.ts` showing as modified with an EMPTY textual diff (a pre-existing CRLF artifact). Never `git add -A`, never revert or normalize another session's paths. List exactly your six paths in `complete_step.modifiedFiles`: the three docs, the two generated files, and the new test.

Call `moe.complete_task` with verification `{ command: 'npm test', exitCode: 0, outputTail: <tail> }` run from `packages/moe-daemon`, and a summary that names the single reconciled rule, the red-to-green transition of the guard test, the linter's qa.md line count, and the fact that skillFiles.ts was regenerated alongside initFiles.ts even though the DoD named only the latter.

No CLAUDE.md conflict: "wrappers are the only git actors" scopes the daemon, not a QA seat. docs/roles/qa.md line 8 (269d3fe, 2026-09-06, measured 1-in-3 completions stranded in the dirty tree) supersedes docs/skills/moe-qa-loop/SKILL.md line 18 (bf3f8fa, 2026-08-29). Reconcile the SKILL to qa.md, keep qa.md's path-scoping recipe canonical, regenerate initFiles.
priorBlockedReason: Planning needs a human authority decision: the task recommends a bounded wait followed by QA self-landing, and docs/roles/qa.md currently instructs that, but CLAUDE.md's Land on every exit rule says wrappers are the only git actors. Cannot submit a speculative plan authorizing QA to create commits or silently replace the requested fallback. Asked in the REPL whether to use a 2-minute wait then worker/governor escalation with wrapper-only landing; awaiting confirmation. Packaging audit also found the honest scope is 6 files (qa.md, qa.reference.md, moe-qa-loop/SKILL.md, generated/initFiles.ts, generated/skillFiles.ts, and one doc-contract test), so the current planning skill calls for a source-policy/test slice plus a linked generated-artifact delivery slice. No files edited or builds/tests run; preserve existing generated/initFiles.ts dirt. Need approved fallback policy and task-scope reconciliation before submission.
planSizeWarnings: Plan touches 6 distinct files (target <=5); plans over 10 are rejected. Small file-disjoint tasks review better and parallelize.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
(1) Reconcile SKILL.md to qa.md (CHOSEN — the governor ruling in reopenReason settles authority: qa.md line 8 from 269d3fe/2026-09-06 supersedes SKILL.md line 18 from bf3f8fa/2026-08-29; qa.md's path-scoping recipe stays canonical). (2) Reconcile qa.md to SKILL.md (unbounded wait) — REJECTED: measured 2026-09-06, one completion in three never gets a wrapper landing at all, so an unbounded wait strands those rows forever. (3) Bounded wait then escalate to worker/governor instead of self-landing — REJECTED: the previous architect session proposed this and blocked on it; the governor ruled that 'wrappers are the only git actors' in CLAUDE.md scopes the daemon, not a QA seat. (4) Split generated-artifact delivery into a second task — REJECTED: the governor ruling names 'regenerate initFiles' as part of this task, and the diff is small.

HOW THE WAIT IS SPENT: do not add a sleep loop. The bounded wait is absorbed by work QA already owes — re-running task.verification and the tests normally exceeds the wrapper's landing window on its own. Re-poll get_context afterwards. This is why the SKILL's step ordering changes, not just its wording.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
GENERATION: `docs/roles/*.md` -> `packages/moe-daemon/src/generated/initFiles.ts` (ROLE_DOCS, keys 'qa.md' / 'qa.reference.md'); `docs/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` -> `packages/moe-daemon/src/generated/skillFiles.ts` (SKILL_FILES, key 'moe-qa-loop/SKILL.md'). BOTH are tracked and BOTH must be regenerated — the DoD names only initFiles.ts, but SKILL.md lives in skillFiles.ts, so leaving it stale would ship the old contradictory text to every IDE user.

I VERIFIED both generated files are currently IN SYNC with their sources (sha12 of LF-normalized, trimEnd'd content matches every embedded `moe-generated: sha=` marker). Regeneration will therefore produce ONLY the intended diffs — no drag-along from other docs.

GENERATORS: `npm run generate-init-files` and `npm run generate-skill-files` (both tsx scripts). `npm run prebuild` runs them but ALSO runs `npm run clean`, which deletes dist/ — avoid it on this shared checkout; call the two generate scripts directly, they produce byte-identical output. Their own error handling already covers the Docker case: each exits 0 with a message when its source docs directory is absent.

MARKERS: role docs get an HTML comment marker prepended; SKILL.md gets a YAML comment INSIDE the frontmatter (loaders require `---` on line 1). Both hash LF-normalized content. This is why the guard test asserts substrings, not full-text equality.

LINTER: `scripts/lint-role-docs.sh` caps docs/roles/{architect,worker,qa}.md at 40 LINES (not chars). qa.md is 25 lines now; *.reference.md is exempt. `npm run lint` needs Git Bash on Windows; `scripts/lint-role-docs.ps1` is the native sibling.

NOT IN SCOPE: `moe-vscode/bundled/docs/roles/qa.md` and the JetBrains sandbox copies are UNTRACKED build artifacts (I checked `git ls-files`) — the gradle build copies from repo root at build time. Do not edit them. A plugin rebuild is a release action, not a code change for this task.
planningNotes.risks:
1. FORBIDDEN-PHRASE FALSE POSITIVE: the guard test asserts the literal strings 'Do NOT wait' and 'wait for it before reviewing' are absent. Do not reintroduce either literal in the new prose (e.g. avoid 'do not wait forever'). Match is case-sensitive on the exact quoted forms from the DoD.

2. THE TEST IS RED UNTIL THE LAST EDIT STEP. It asserts on the GENERATED constants, so the doc edits alone will not turn it green — only the regeneration step will. That is intentional (it is the staleness guard). Do not 'fix' the test when it stays red after editing the docs.

3. CRLF: this checkout is Windows. `git status` already shows initFiles.ts as modified with an EMPTY textual diff — a pre-existing LF/CRLF artifact, not your change and not a defect. Do not normalize, revert, or 'clean' it. The guard test must LF-normalize any file it reads from disk before comparing.

4. 40-LINE CAP: qa.md is 25 lines. The replacement bullet must stay ONE line (the file's existing style is one long bullet per rule) so the count barely moves. Run the linter before completing.

5. SHARED CHECKOUT: 9 dirty paths belong to other sessions. Never `git add -A`, never revert them. Report exactly your own paths in complete_step.modifiedFiles.

6. DO NOT run `npm run build` / `npm run prebuild` in the daemon package — `clean` deletes dist/ out from under anything using this checkout. Use the two generate scripts, then `npx tsc --noEmit` for the typecheck.

7. SCOPE: this is the Wave 0 interim rule. Do not design or reference attempt/candidate/receipt mechanics (Wave 1) beyond the single 'interim until Wave 1 lands' sentence in the reference doc.
